question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

To prime the pump

options.text: Encourage the growth or action of something’

solution:
The correct answer is: **Encourage the growth or action of something**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom '**To prime the pump**' means to stimulate or encourage the initial growth or action of something. (किसी चीज़ की प्रारंभिक वृद्धि या क्रिया को उत्तेजित या प्रोत्साहित करना)

 
 
• **For example**: *I added some fuel to the car's engine to prime the pump before starting it.*
 
 
 
• It is often used in reference to economic activity, where priming the pump refers to increasing government spending to stimulate economic growth.
 
• The phrase is believed to have originated from the practice of pumping water from a well, where priming the pump involved adding water to the pump to create suction and start the flow of water.
 
• This idiom can also be used metaphorically in non-economic contexts, such as encouraging creativity or productivity in a team.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Manipulate someone to achieve success**" is not an accurate meaning of the idiom "to prime the pump."
 
• "**To use a pump efficiently**" is not an accurate meaning of the idiom "to prime the pump."
 
• "**Ask others to be ambitious**" is not an accurate meaning of the idiom "to prime the pump."
